title: How Telangana Got Back 550 Acres in Miyapur Worth About Rs 50,000 Crore
excerpt: A Supreme Court verdict ended the dispute over Miyapur's survey numbers 100 and 101 in the state's favour. The Hindu's explainer traces how the land was claimed, and Chief Minister Revanth Reddy says recovered land worth Rs 1.5 lakh crore has been protected across seven sites.
body:
• The Supreme Court ruled that all rights over 550 acres of government poramboke land in Miyapur, Rangareddy district — survey numbers 100 and 101 — vest entirely with the Telangana government, ending a dispute the state says ran for more than two decades.
  • Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy put the land's value at about Rs 50,000 crore; The Hindu's explainer puts the recovered land at over Rs 55,000 crore.
  • The chief minister alleges the land was targeted through manipulated Dharani land records and falsified revenue records — allegations against the previous BRS government that have not been independently established.
  • A cabinet sub-committee on resource mobilisation will examine monetising recovered land, with proceeds proposed for irrigation, education, healthcare and welfare, the government says; no auction has been scheduled.

The land is 550 acres in Miyapur, on Hyderabad's western edge, in survey numbers 100 and 101. The Supreme Court has ruled that every right over it belongs to the Telangana government, The Hindu explained in its account of the verdict. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, announcing the ruling to the media from New Delhi on Friday, October 30, called it a historic judgment and thanked the court for ensuring the land was not alienated from public ownership.

What was decided

The ruling affirms that the Miyapur acreage is government poramboke land — land recorded as state-owned — and that all rights over it vest entirely with the state, according to Nation Press's account of the verdict. The chief minister directed officials to begin protective measures for the land immediately. The government estimates the parcel's value at about Rs 50,000 crore; The Hindu's explainer headline puts the figure at over Rs 55,000 crore. Either way, it is among the most valuable single parcels of government land in the Hyderabad region.

How the state says the land was targeted

The dispute, the government says, stemmed from attempts by private individuals and investors to occupy the government acreage under the cover of colony layouts — a pattern the chief minister said intensified after Telangana's formation in 2014, when real-estate demand around Hyderabad sharpened the appetite for unencumbered public parcels. Revanth Reddy alleged that the methods used included manipulation of the Dharani land-records portal, falsification of revenue records and pressure on officials to reclassify government parcels. Dharani was launched in 2020 to digitise Telangana's revenue records and curb exactly these kinds of encroachments.

The chief minister accused former chief minister K. Chandrashekar Rao, his relative Damodar Rao and 'Goldstone' Prasad of attempting to grab the land, Devdiscourse reported. These are the chief minister's allegations, made at a press conference; they have not been independently established, and the reports of the verdict carried no response from the BRS leaders named.

Seven sites, Rs 1.5 lakh crore claimed protected

Miyapur is the largest single item in a wider claim. The chief minister said his government has protected public land worth approximately Rs 1.5 lakh crore through legal battles across seven major sites since taking office. The list he gave includes 400 acres at Kancha Gachibowli, 450 acres at Mamidipalli, 140 acres of forest land at Sahebnagar Kalan in Hayathnagar mandal, 36 acres at Kondapur worth roughly Rs 3,600 crore, 143 acres at Manchirevula — 50 of them allocated for the Young India Police School — 106 acres of forest land in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district and 600 acres in Bhadradri Kothagudem district.

What happens to the land now

The government says recovered land will not lie idle, because idle government land invites fresh encroachment. Forest department land will be returned to the Forest Department and revenue land to the Revenue Department. A cabinet sub-committee on resource mobilisation will study whether parcels should be monetised; the chief minister has said proceeds would go to irrigation projects, education, healthcare, Dalit and tribal welfare and Indiramma housing. No auction date has been announced — the proposal must first be examined by that sub-committee, so any sale is a decision still to come, not a schedule.

nri_angle: Hyderabad land values are a live concern for NRI property holders in Telangana; a Supreme Court ruling that 550 acres of Miyapur poramboke land was always the state's — and allegations that the Dharani records portal was manipulated — bear directly on how safely land records can be trusted.
